I asked him why I could not see the Ethereum, and he explained that it might have to do with me having another crypto account elsewhere. I told him that I didnt understand why that would affect the ability to transfer cryptos from one account to another. He agreed that it was unlikely, but stated it might be a possibility. To : Complaints Department, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau From : XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX : XX/XX/2024 Re : Chase Bank fraud against us ; Chase Bank Case # XXXX I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding my treatment by Chase Bank . Chase has treated me very unfairly and abused the trust I placed in them. I have reported them to the XXXX XXXX XXXX, and also to the FBI. I am considering legal action against Chase for their unfair treatment of me and for their violations of various federal laws and regulations. I feel Chase is taking advantage of our ages and difficulty in understanding complex financial issues due to the language barrier.

Neither my husband nor I had ever done wire transfers before from Chase or any other bank, and certainly not to any international locations, as these were. All 5 wires were processed within a 30-minute period of time on the same day, and neither my husband nor I authorized any of them, either on a paper form or electronically. It would take 5 separate authorizations to do this over this short period of time ; we did not provide even one. Chase refuses to provide any sort of proof that we did. Theyve just told us that we authorized the wires and our case is closed without any additional information other than essentially, we think you authorized the wires. It seems a gross breach of Chases duty under federal law to monitor for potentially fraudulent transactions to allow multiple wires over a short period of time to international locations from an XXXX customers account where none had ever been done before.

To make matters worse, the amount of these wires exceeded the amount of money we had in our checking account. Without our consent, Chase transferred money from our savings account to cover the wires. When opening our accounts ( and well before this fraud ), we specifically refused any sort of automatic transfers between accounts to cover overdrafts. Chase tells us that transfers are automatic to cover wires regardless of whether we allowed the bank to do it or not. This seems incredibly unfair, and seems like theft to me. Chase refuses to provide any sort of proof we opted in to overdraft transfers, or authorized a transfer on that day. Im told this is a violation of federal Regulation E, as the bank is required to provide documentation when they deny our dispute of the transfer between accounts. I know it is also a violation to require us to file a police report before processing our dispute, as Chase did, as detailed below. 

The fraudulent wires were all done on XX/XX/2024. While looking at my account to print documents for taxes on that same day, I noticed a fraud alert on their website for my account. I called my husband immediately and he saw that the majority of our funds had disappeared from our account. He called the Chase fraud department ( I got their number from their website ). He was on hold for 5 minutes, then after becoming frustrated he decided to call the Chase branch on XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, AZ, but no one answered the phone. He then called the Chase branch on XXXX XXXX in XXXX, AZ, and had a 32-minute conversation with a very helpful employee to report the fraud. She pulled up our account and could see that money was in the process of exiting our account. She expressed surprise that nobody could stop the fraud that was happening before our eyes. She then stated not to worry and we would get our money back, which was very reassuring. She then transferred him to another department, where he had to explain the entire situation again. We were very frustrated that no one seemed to approach our money disappearing with any sense of urgency. The gentleman from the fraud department ended up hanging up on my husband. Apparently, he was only on the job for two weeks. The really maddening thing is additional wire transfers went out of our account AFTER we had these calls with the bank. Chase knew we had not authorized any wires ; yet more wires came out after they were on notice.

In a panic, I jumped into my car and drove to the Chase branch on XXXX XXXX XXXX. A teller at the branch told me I had to file a police report before I could make a claim to the Chase Fraud Department, which seemed odd to me. Couldnt they stop the fraud, or at least start to investigate, before I had to file a police report? They did not even offer to shut off the ability to make further wires. She gave me the wrong address to the police department, but I finally made it over to the police department. I received a police report number and called the Chase Fraud Department. The Chase Fraud Department never did ask me for the police report number, which was odd since they told me they required this before I could file a dispute. This seems like a waste of time to me, since the bank could have been working to prevent further fraudulent wires from being done. I know now also that the bank can not make me get a police report before they investigate the transfer of funds from my savings to my checking account. 

On XX/XX/2024, I went back to the Chase branch on XXXX XXXX XXXX, but was told I had to come back later to speak to XXXX, which I did. XXXX closed our accounts and opened new ones, ordered new credit cards, then said I would have to come back on the next Tuesday ( Monday was a holiday ) with my husband XXXX to complete the investigation into what had happened. 

On XX/XX/2024, we spent 4 hours with XXXX. We were told that the case had already been closed, as the bank is saying we authorized the wire transfers. I told her we have never wired funds from our account, we dont use wires, and we did not authorize these wires. In addition, the majority of the funds were in our savings account which had been transferred to our checking account to complete the wires. We never authorized any sort of transfer from our savings, either when we opened our accounts or to do these wires that day. In fact, we specifically declined overdraft protection when we opened the account. She just kept saying that the fraud department said we authorized everything, and wouldnt provide any explanation or other information or documentation, even when we repeatedly asked. 

On XX/XX/2024, I went to the Chase branch in XXXX XXXX, AZ, and spoke with XXXX, a personal banker. After explaining our entire situation, XXXX saw at this point all of our money was gone from both checking and savings, and that our checking account was now in a negative balance due to bank fees applied to our account. XXXX was able to reopen our case, but she requested a report from IT. It seems incredibly unfair to charge us {$120.00} in fees to perform wires that we did not authorize ( which they have refused to refund, also without explanation ) that put our checking account in a negative balance. Do we now have to pay overdraft fees too since Chase charged us wire fees? 

On XX/XX/2024, I called XXXX at the Chase branch on XXXX XXXX XXXX again to tell her that all of my emails and contacts on my cell phone are gone. She told me that she thinks my cell phone was somehow mirrored and someone else authorized the wires using our credentials. She advised me to go get a new cell phone, new phone number and to not transfer anything from the old phone to the new phone. She also advised that I close out all of my email accounts and open new email accounts. I did all that was advised, although this seemed to be just her personal opinion. There was nothing from the Chase fraud department or IT department saying anything like this. This also seems to contradict what the bank was telling me if my cell phone was mirrored, then it seems the bank thinks the wires were authorized by someone other than my husband or me. So why is the bank closing the case and saying we authorized them? 

I also contacted all the credit bureaus and place a freeze and fraud alerts on my credit report just to be safe. I also called the Social Security Office and placed a fraud alert on our records.

Again, they refuse to provide any sort of proof that this is allowed, or that we authorized it. I know that we are entitled to documentation of transfers where there isnt an automatic agreement. I trusted Chase with my life savings. This again was ignored. 

I think Chase is ignoring our requests for more information and documentation, even when we know were entitled to it. I think they are just trying to get us to go away, especially since were both XXXX  and dont speak English very well. Not only is this treatment not right, its against federal laws banks must follow. 

If we have to get a subpoena to get any information, we will do this. We will also sue the bank for their treatment of us as XXXX, non-English native customers, and for their violations of federal banking laws. 

Please provide whatever help you can to us to get to the bottom of this. We did not authorize these wires. We just want our funds back.

Subsequently, a second charge of {$2600.00} was taken without permission on XX/XX/XXXX and was declined by Amex for exceeding my available balance. Following this, XXXX more fraudulent charges of {$1000.00}, {$500.00}, and {$250.00} were transacted successfully. Despite the initial decline, no action was taken to protect the account, allowing the fraudulent charges to proceed until the account was maxed out and there was no more available credit. Additionally, over a dozen attempts to charge various amounts were blocked by Amex. These charges were reported in good faith, as XXXX XXXX was found to be impersonating a contractor and has a criminal record. Amex conducted a thorough investigation and reversed all the fraudulent charges. A criminal complaint has been filed against XXXX XXXX with XXXX XXXX from the Arizona Registrar of Contractors ( Case XXXX ). 

Even though I was a victim of financial fraud, the account has always been maintained in good standing and Amex bills have been paid on time. Due to XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX  ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), the stress and complexity of this situation had a disproportionate impact. According to the National Institutes of Health ( NIH ), symptoms of XXXX can include irritability, agitation, and mood swings, particularly when exacerbated by stress. In the haste to report the crime, language that could be perceived as offensive may have been unintentionally used. If any communications were construed as abusive, a sincere apology is extended. It was never the intention to disrespect or harm anyone. Actions were driven by the urgency and frustration of being a victim of a significant financial crime. XXXX and XXXX are currently being managed with the help of medical professionals. 

An employee named XXXX indicated that the alleged abuse took place on a call dated XX/XX/2024, and filed a claim ( XXXX ) to allow the back team to review the call. However, no calls were made to Amex on that date. During this time, prank phone calls were being received from XXXX XXXX and the police had to be contacted regarding his behavior. It seems possible that XXXX XXXX may have contacted the bank on that date. When called back, a different time frame was given, and the representative refused to provide the date of the alleged activity. Instead of educating on what the alleged abusive behavior was to curtail it in the future or allowing reference to the specific conversation, it was stated that a subpoena would be required for that information. 

The lack of clear communication and transparency regarding the specific policy allegedly violated is concerning. While it is understood that American Express reserves the right to " cancel or suspend any feature on your Account '' at its discretion, such actions should be taken fairly and transparently. The Cardmember Agreement provided does not list abusive language as a reason for cancellation, making it difficult to understand the basis for this action. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), specifically Regulation Z ( XXXX and XXXX ), creditors are required to clearly and conspicuously disclose terms and conditions, including any circumstances under which an account may be closed. The enforcement of an undisclosed " moral clause '' related to abusive language appears to be a violation of TILA 's requirement for transparency and clear disclosure. 

Additionally, effective XX/XX/2024, American Express is amending the Cardmember Agreement to include the ability to cancel or suspend accounts " at any time and for any reason. '' This clause was not part of the agreement at the time the account was canceled, suggesting that the current action may not be supported by the terms of the agreement in effect when the decision was made. Furthermore, as of today, XX/XX/2024, the Card Membership Agreement still lists the available limit as {$8000.00}, which contradicts the letter dated XX/XX/2024, stating the account was canceled. 

Multiple representatives stated that there was no way to appeal the decision and that it was final. This contradicts the terms outlined in the Cardmember Agreement, which specifies the method to appeal any decision. If the Cardmember Agreement includes an appeal process, American Express is required to inform cardholders of this process in its communication regarding adverse decisions. The absence of such information in the notice received could be considered a violation of TILAs requirements for clear and conspicuous disclosure and may also constitute a breach of contract and a violation of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing. As such, the failure to follow its own stated procedures and provide a clear appeal process means that the decision to cancel the account is procedurally incorrect and invalid, irrespective of the alleged language. 

Moreover, the Americans with Disabilities Act ( ADA ) and Section XXXX of the Rehabilitation Act require that people with XXXX be provided with reasonable accommodations and not be discriminated against. These laws mandate clear and effective communication with individuals with XXXX, ensuring that procedures are fair and transparent. As a person with XXXX and XXXX, membership in a protected class should be considered, and interactions with Amex should consider the impact of these conditions. 

The notice regarding the federal Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) states that creditors are prohibited from discriminating against credit applicants on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act. According to 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( a ), discrimination based on XXXX, including XXXX and XXXX, can be considered discriminatory. I told the supervisor it can't be a Paypal issue, as it was NOT a " Pay through Paypal '' funded transaction, it was done as a direct payment using my card, not through Paypal. Key amenities listed, including functioning air conditioning, hot water, and a usable kitchen grill, were either inoperable or nonexistent. We believe this to be a strategic fraudulent inducement to purchase services, which were materially not rendered. Discover is failing to stand behind their anti-fraud guarantee, and XXXX XXXX is less than helpful. We have no intention of paying for this charge in full, as we incurred extra cost on the trip due to these issues.

For example, the listing showed an inviting living space and functioning outdoor grill, but the actual condition of the home was poor. Appliances like the dishwasher and refrigerator were broken and unusable.

We were left with no usable bathroom, and every time we used the shower, it flooded, causing additional damage and foul odors throughout the suite .

Health and Safety Violations : The flooded bathroom floor emitted a repulsive odor, and the water that pooled had a brownish tint, potentially containing sewage or human XXXX. This posed a serious health risk to me and my companions. 
Air Conditioning Misrepresentation : The listing also promised air conditioning, a critical feature given the hot climate. However, the air conditioning was hard-set by the host, and we had no control over the temperature. Additionally, the guest suite , where we spent most of our time, did not have any air conditioning at all. 

Financial Losses : Due to the condition of the rental, my group and I had to purchase over {$500.00} worth of groceries from XXXX, which were ruined because the refrigerator was not airtight and leaked all over the kitchen floor. We incurred additional expenses to rebook alternative lodging for the remaining days of our trip, as the property was uninhabitable.

Discover should be standing behind their card members, and not putting me in the middle of issues with services not rendered, or services not received with a fraudulent merchant.

This experience has not only caused me financial losses but has also disrupted what was meant to be a relaxing vacation. I would greatly appreciate the CFPBs help in resolving this matter and holding XXXX accountable for their unethical and deceptive business practices.

Therefore, there was no legitimate reason to close the account. I tried to reason with the Citibank Customer Service Representatives ( CSR ) and Supervisors for several hours on the phone for a reasonable resolution but to no avail. I believe that this is a common tactic of corporate stonewalling by deterring the consumer to come to a resolution due to many layers of deterrence. This situation is basically a large corporation ( Citibank ) stealing from the consumer ( me, and potentially others with the same situation ). In summary, closing my account and forfeiting my points is effectively theft by Citibank. 


Potential UDAAP violations : While this issue does not pertain to the collection of a consumer debt, the following describes how this situation meets all three of the Applicable Standards for UDAAPs. 

XXXX. Unfair Acts or Practices The Dodd-Frank Act prohibits conduct that constitutes an unfair act or practice. An act or practice is unfair when : ( XXXX ) It causes or is likely to cause substantial injury to consumers ; ( XXXX ) The injury is not reasonably avoidable by consumers ; and ( XXXX ) The injury is not outweighed by countervailing benefits to consumers or to competition. 

The injury is monetary, in the amount of {$1100.00}. I couldnt avoid the injury, as they closed my account and took my points/cash value. 

XXXX. Deceptive Acts or Practices The Dodd-Frank Act also prohibits conduct that constitutes a deceptive act or practice. An act or practice is deceptive when : ( XXXX ) The act or practice misleads or is likely to mislead the consumer ; ( XXXX ) The consumers interpretation is reasonable under the circumstances; and ( XXXX ) The misleading act or practice is material. 

The deceptive act or practice is the stealing ( forfeiture ) of my points for no reason, when I had an open credit card with no delinquencies and good credit. 


XXXX. Abusive Acts or Practices The Dodd-Frank Act also prohibits conduct that constitutes an abusive act or practice. An act or practice is abusive when it : ( XXXX ) Materially interferes with the ability of a consumer to understand a term or condition of a consumer financial product or service; or ( XXXX ) Takes unreasonable advantage of ( A ) a consumers lack of understanding of the material risks, costs, or conditions of the product or service; ( B ) a consumers inability to protect his or her interests in selecting or using a consumer financial product or service; or ( C ) a consumers reasonable reliance on a covered person to act in his or her interests. 

The abusive act or practice is theft of my points that have a cash value of {$1100.00}. 

Additional Details : Prior to filing this complaint, I tried very hard to come to what I thought was a very reasonable resolution to the issue. I simply wanted Citibank to either reinstate my credit card with my points or issue me the cash value of those points at {$1100.00}. As previously stated, I accumulated the points over a period more than 10 years. In XX/XX/XXXX, I called a Citibank CSR and inquired about my points. During that conversation, the CSR informed me that the points never expire. In addition, I was never informed that my account would be closing. In XX/XX/XXXX, I tried to access my account to use some of my points, however, I could not access my points. I then spent over 4 hours talking to several Citibank CSRs and Supervisors over 3 days, from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX. The last person I spoke to was Senior Account Supervisor with Citi Cards in Arizona, with the name of XXXX. In summary, all the CSRs and Supervisors told me that the account had been closed, the points had been forfeited, and there was nothing that they could do. I repeatedly tried to escalate to higher supervisors, but at some point, they refused to escalate it anymore. Here is where I refer to the strategy of corporate stonewalling the strategy of making consumers feel they have no options because the supervisors just basically disregard their reasonable requests. In addition, I strongly believe that this is corporate theft, as CitiBank had no legitimate reason to close my credit card that had an expiration date of XX/XX/XXXX. Again, I have strong credit and never had any delinquencies. 

I bring this to the attention of the CFPB not only to recoup the {$1100.00} that I am entitled to, but to highlight this very unfair practice that could be impacting other consumers. These unfair practices should result in civil money penalties and restitution. 

I am only seeking from Citibank a fair resolution to this issue, which would be one of two options : XXXX ) Reopen the credit card, with my point reestablished, or XXXX ) Issue me a check for the cash value of my points, which is {$1100.00}.

Consumer Name : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Company Complained Against : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . 
Product : Credit Card or Prepaid Card Issue : Other problem with a credit card Complaint Narrative : I am filing this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . for engaging in deceptive, misleading, and materially incomplete disclosures concerning the origination and management of my consumer credit card account.

1. Material Omission Regarding Securitization : At the time I opened my Chase credit card account, I was never informed that my future receivables ( debt obligations ) would be pooled, securitized, and sold into investment instruments through a public trust ( specifically, the Chase Issuance Trust ).

This is a material fact which, if disclosed, would have influenced my decision to accept the credit terms.

Failure to disclose this violates the disclosure requirements of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA, 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ), which mandates that material terms affecting consumer obligations must be disclosed fully and fairly. 

Supporting Case Law : XXXX XXXX XXXX Mortgage XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) : Even small undisclosed fees or material terms violate TILA if they affect a consumers ability to make an informed decision. 

XXXX. Deceptive and Unfair Practices ( UDAAP ) : Chases practice of selling consumer debts without disclosing this to consumers is a deceptive omission and an unfair practice under the Dodd-Frank Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ( a ) ), which prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) in connection with consumer financial products.

Supporting Case Law : FTC v. IFC Credit Corp., 543 F. Supp. 2d 925 ( N.D. Ill. 2008 ) : Courts have held that failing to disclose material information related to finance contracts constitutes deceptive and unfair conduct.

3. Denial of the Right to Know True Creditor ( Assignment Notice Failure ) : Under 15 U.S.C. 1641 ( g ), when a creditor sells, assigns, or otherwise transfers ownership of a debt, the consumer must be notified.

By securitizing and transferring my account into an investment trust without notification, Chase violated my right to know the identity of my true creditor. 

Supporting Case Law : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, L.P., XXXX XXXX XXXX ( S.D. XXXX. XXXX ) : Failure to notify a consumer of an assignment of debt violates the disclosure requirements of TILA 1641 ( g ).

4. Injury and Financial Harm : I suffered harm by unknowingly entering a relationship where my debt obligations are owned or controlled by third parties. I was denied the opportunity to negotiate terms appropriate for this additional risk and exposure. 

XXXX. Chain of Title and Ownership Risk : The legal ownership of my obligation is now clouded by securitization. If enforcement becomes necessary, it is unclear whether Chase or any successor trust would have standing to enforce the obligation. 

Supporting Case Law : XXXX Bank XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Mass. XXXX ) : The court held that securitized assets must have proper, clear documentation to maintain enforceability. Failure to properly disclose or document assignment harms borrowers legal defenses. 

XXXX. Evidence Submitted : Chase Cardmember Agreement ( showing lack of securitization disclosure ), Chase Issuance Trust Prospectus ( confirming receivable securitization ), Signed Declaration under 28 U.S.C. 1746 affirming the truth of my statements.

7. Relief Requested : Full investigation into JPMorgan Chase Banks origination, disclosure, and assignment practices, Enforcement actions to ensure future compliance with disclosure laws, Monetary and/or equitable relief based on harm caused by deceptive omissions, Corrective actions mandating disclosure of securitization practices to consumers at account origination.

This formal complaint regarding Capital Ones mishandling of a fraud investigation, the unauthorized acceptance of charges from the merchant XXXX, and the subsequent wrongful closure of my credit card account. This issue is not only a violation of your advertised {$0.00} Fraud Liability policy but also contravenes multiple federal and state laws, resulting in significant financial hardship, reputational damage, and psychological harm. 

Summary of Events : On Wednesday, XX/XX/year>, I was informed by a Capital XXXX representative that XXXX had attempted to charge my account three ( 3 ) times. I was further assured that blocking the token ID, issuing a new credit card, and changing account information would prevent any further charges from the merchant. 
Despite these assurances, a charge from XXXX in the amount of {$1900.00} was allowed to post to my account on XX/XX/year>. 
I immediately reported this transaction as fraudulent. A fraud claim was initiated under XXXX XXXX XXXX. 
I received closure documentation via the Capital One mobile app on XX/XX/year>, indicating the fraud case was closed in favor of the merchant. This contradicted multiple representatives who told me the investigation was still ongoing. 
Capital Ones fraud resolution letter clearly states that you sided with the merchant without offering me any opportunity to rebut their submission, violating my right to due process under applicable consumer protection laws. 
A Capital One Fraud Manager named XXXX ( Badge ID : XXXX ) misrepresented that the merchants documentation included a copy of my photo ID. Upon receiving the documentation myself, no such ID was present, confirming that Capital One falsely represented key evidence. 
I was then told by another fraud team member, XXXX ( Badge ID : XXXX ), that I am not entitled to view or contest the merchants rebuttal, further violating my rights as a consumer. 
As a direct result of Capital Ones willful negligence and misconduct, I was forced to contact the merchant myself and my account was wrongfully closed, compounding the financial, emotional, and reputational damage.

Legal Violations and Supporting Statutes : Federal Laws Violated : 1. Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S. Code 1666 You failed to properly investigate and resolve a disputed charge within 2 billing cycles ( 90 days ), and you did not provide a meaningful opportunity for me to contest the merchants claim.

You violated my right to dispute unauthorized charges and withheld the rebuttal evidence, which constitutes unfair billing practices.

2. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S. Code 1601 et seq.

By allowing an unauthorized charge to post despite prior notification of fraud, you violated the disclosure and billing requirements of TILA.

3. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S. Code 1693 et seq.

Failure to block further charges after a claim of fraud may also constitute a violation of consumer protections under EFTA, which requires prompt and accurate resolution of reported fraud.

4. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ( a ) If this account closure negatively impacted my credit report, this would represent a violation of the duty to report accurate information and to conduct reasonable investigations upon disputes.

Arizona State Laws Violated : 1. Arizona Consumer Fraud Act, A.R.S. 44-1522 Capital One made false assurances that no further charges could occur and failed to disclose the true nature of its fraud resolution process.

Misrepresentation and concealment of facts ( such as the false claim of having my ID ) fall under deceptive business practices.

2. Arizona Revised Statutes 13-2310 Fraudulent schemes and artifices If Capital One intentionally misrepresented documentation or denied my right to view rebuttal materials, this may qualify as a fraudulent scheme.

Utah State Laws Violated : 1. Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act ( UCSPA ), Utah Code 13-11-4 ( 1 ) Misrepresenting the effect of account security changes and then allowing a charge contradicts protection from unfair or deceptive acts or practices in consumer transactions.

2. Utah Code 7-16-3 Protections for financial institution account holders Financial institutions must exercise reasonable care in protecting account holder assets, which Capital One failed to do.

To Whom It May Concern : I am disputing Capital Ones reporting of late-payment entries on the above account. Those entries are inaccurate and/or legally noncompliant and must be corrected or deleted.

Why the reporting is unlawful 1. Accuracy duty ( Furnishers ). The FCRA prohibits a furnisher from providing information it knowsor has reasonable cause to believeis inaccurate, and requires prompt correction/updates if previously furnished information is not complete or accurate. 
2. Investigation duty ( after a dispute ). Upon receiving notice of a dispute ( directly from me or via a CRA ), Capital One must conduct a reasonable investigation, review all relevant information, and report the results ; if the data is inaccurate, incomplete, or can not be verified, Capital One must modify, delete, or block the information and notify all nationwide CRAs to which it furnished the item.

3. Obsolete/too old to report. Adverse items ( including collections and other negative information such as late payments ) generally may not be reported beyond seven years ( with the 7-year period for a delinquent account running from the Date of First Delinquency as defined by statute ). If any late-payment entry is beyond this limit, it is illegal to continue furnishing it.

4. Disputed-status duty. While a dispute is pending, any furnishing of the item must include notice that the information is disputed.

5. Direct-dispute rules ( Regulation V ). Because Im disputing directly with the furnisher, Capital One must reasonably investigate my dispute so long as it concerns my liability, terms, performance, or other account info that bears on creditworthinessand must notify me if it deems the dispute frivolous, within five business days, with reasons and whats needed to investigate.

Furnisher accuracy & correction duties. FCRA 623 ( a ) bars furnishers from reporting information they know or reasonably should know is inaccurate and requires them to correct/update incomplete or inaccurate info.

Duties after a dispute. When notified of a dispute, furnishers must investigate, review all relevant information, report results, and if the info is inaccurate/incomplete/unverifiable, they must modify, delete, or block itand notify all CRAs to which it was furnished. 
CRA reinvestigation timelines ( helpful benchmark ). CRAs must complete reinvestigations within 30 days ( extendable to 45 in limited circumstances ), and notify you of results.

Direct disputes ( Reg V, 12 C.F.R. 1022.43 ). A furnisher must reasonably investigate direct disputes about liability, terms, performance, or other account info ; if it calls a dispute frivolous, it must tell you within 5 business days with reasons and whats needed to proceed.

Seven-year obsolescence rule. Negative items ( including collections and other adverse data ) generally cant be reported more than seven years from the Date of First Delinquency ; for delinquent accounts, the 7-year period runs from DOFD + 180 days.

Marking disputes. If a consumer disputes accuracy/completeness, any furnishing of that item must identify it as disputed. 
COVID-19 accommodation rule ( if applicable ). During covered periods, accounts current at the start of an accommodation must be reported as current for as long as the accommodation is in place.

Important reality check : The FCRA does not prohibit reporting truthful late payments. The law prohibits inaccurate, obsolete, or unverified negative reporting and requires proper investigations and dispute handling. The letter above targets those legal violations.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Subject : Deceptive Trade Practices, Unauthorized Withdrawals, and Concealment of Material Account Information by Sezzle , Inc. 
To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this formal complaint against Sezzle , Inc. for unauthorized withdrawals, deceptive trade practices, and concealment of account information that caused significant financial loss, undue stress, and years of confusion. Sezzles actions violated my rights as a consumer and small-business owner and constitute serious breaches of federal consumer financial protection laws. 
Background and Timeline of Events In XXXX, while operating my business XXXX XXXX XXXX, I applied for a Sezzle merchant account. From the time of application onward, my Sezzle dashboard consistently displayed Application Denied. Based on this clear representation, I reasonably concluded that my application had not been approved and that no funds were being processed through Sezzle.

Relying on this information, I ceased all attempts to use Sezzles platform. Over the years, I logged into the account multiple times out of curiosity after receiving various emails from Sezzle ; yet the dashboard still displayed Application Denied. At no point did Sezzle communicate that an active merchant account existed or that any funds were being held. 
Unauthorized Monthly Withdrawals and Hidden Account Despite the Application Denied status, Sezzle repeatedly withdrew {$300.00} per month in so-called merchant inactivity fees, without my knowledge, consent, or awareness that a balance existed. Over time, these withdrawals totaled {$4200.00}. 
It was not until XXXX, after receiving repeated emails about inactivity fees, that I contacted Sezzle support seeking answers. Only then did they disclose, for the first time, that there was a second merchant account associated with my profile that had been approved and was processing funds. This second account was hidden behind a small drop-down menu in the dashboard ; something I had no reason to check since the interface continually defaulted to the Application Denied account.

After I began questioning these charges, Sezzle quietly altered its dashboard interface. The Application Denied message was removed, and the second account suddenly appeared as an option in a drop-down list. This change, occurring only after I raised concerns, is strong evidence that Sezzle was aware its previous interface was misleading and deceptive. 
Dates and Details of Unauthorized Withdrawals Sezzle unlawfully withdrew {$300.00} from my account on the following dates ( documented in email notifications and records ) : XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  These recurring, unauthorized charges total {$4200.00}. 
Although Sezzle eventually permitted me to withdraw the remaining balance of {$2600.00}, they have refused to refund the numerous {$300.00} fees unlawfully taken. 

Violations of Consumer Protection Law Sezzles actions represent serious violations of federal consumer financial protection law and deceptive business practices, including : Material Misrepresentation : The Application Denied message misled me into believing no account existed and that no transactions were occurring. 

Omission of Critical Information : Sezzle failed to disclose that a second, active account was associated with my business. 

Unauthorized Withdrawals : Monthly deductions were taken without my knowledge, consent, or awareness of any balance. 

Deceptive Concealment : The sudden change to the dashboard interface, only after I complained, strongly suggests a deliberate attempt to obscure deceptive practices. 

These actions deprived me of the ability to manage, close, or even monitor my account, directly resulting in financial loss and significant emotional distress. 

Financial and Emotional Impact This situation has been profoundly time-consuming, stressful, and damaging. Over the course of several years, I have spent countless hours contacting Sezzle support, digging through records, and trying to understand why I was receiving emails about inactivity fees when my dashboard said my account was denied. 
The discovery that Sezzle had been quietly withdrawing {$300.00} every month without my knowledge, and that a second account existed the entire time ; has caused immense frustration and XXXX. Their conduct undermined my trust in financial technology platforms and disrupted my ability to operate my business effectively. 

Relief Requested I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : Conduct a full investigation into Sezzle , Inc. for deceptive trade practices, unauthorized withdrawals, and concealment of material account information. 

Require Sezzle to refund the full {$4200.00} in unauthorized withdrawals plus statutory interest, calculated from the date of each withdrawal. 

Direct Sezzle to issue the refund via direct deposit to the verified bank account currently on file ( the same account used for the {$2600.00} disbursement ). 

Ensure Sezzle permanently closes the merchant account associated with XXXX XXXX XXXX upon resolution. 


Consider appropriate enforcement action to prevent Sezzle from continuing these harmful practices against other consumers. 


Additional Documentation and Communications Due to the volume and size of supporting evidence, including more than 25 emails and chat transcripts exchanged between myself and Sezzles support team, I'm not able to upload all documentation through this online portal. 

This complaint is about far more than a billing dispute. It exposes a pattern of deceptive conduct and unauthorized financial activity by a company entrusted with handling consumers and merchants money. Sezzle misrepresented the status of my account, concealed material information, withdrew funds without authorization, and then altered its interface to obscure the truth, all of which resulted in significant financial harm and years of unnecessary stress. 
I urge the CFPB to investigate this matter thoroughly, hold Sezzle accountable under the law, and require full restitution with interest.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint because JPMorgan Chase presented me with what appeared to be a firm approval for a Chase Sapphire XXXX credit card inside my secure Chase login. The messaging stated explicitly : Youre already approved for a Chase Sapphire XXXX card. 

This was not framed as a pre-qualification, pre-approval, or invitation to apply. The wording already approved has a very specific and unambiguous meaning to consumers : that a creditor has already completed an underwriting decision and is extending a firm approval.

Key Misleading Elements : 1. Chase used the phrase already approved, not pre-approved or prequalified. 
The difference is material and significant. Already approved communicates a credit decision, not a conditional one.

2. Chases acceptance page did NOT use the word applyit used the word ACCEPT. 
On the disclosures page, I was required to check a box stating, Ive read and agree to the above, followed by a button labeled Accept. 
Nowhere did Chase indicate that I was applying or that underwriting was still pending. The interface strongly implied that I was merely accepting terms for an account already approved.

3. The fine print does not cure this deception. 
Small-print legalese stating that Chase may be unable to grant this product in limited circumstances is insufficient. 
Both the CFPB and FTC have repeatedly found that prominent statements can not be contradicted or weakened by fine print. A reasonable consumer relies on the clear, bold text presented to them, especially inside a secure authenticated banking environment. 

4. Chase did not request any standard information normally required to submit a credit card application ( SSN, DOB, Income, Address, Employment, etc ). At no point was I asked to provide or update this information.

5. Chase denied the card immediately after I accepted. 
Despite being told I was already approved, Chase denied the application. This is deceptive regardless of embedded disclaimers. It indicates that Chase induced me to proceed under false pretenses.

6. I incurred a hard credit inquiry based on a misleading representation.

This harms my credit profile and access to future credit products. I would not have proceeded had Chase not stated affirmatively that I was already approved.

7. The interface design appears intentionally deceptive.

The use of already approved The absence of any apply language The requirement to accept rather than submit an application Together these elements create the appearance of a firm offer.

Chases conduct may constitute
a violation of the Consumer Financial Protection Acts UDAAP prohibitions because : The claim already approved is factually false The wording and interface materially mislead a reasonable consumer Fine print can not cure a direct contradiction or deceptive headline A consumer suffered concrete harm ( hard inquiry, misuse of credit information ) The conduct appears systemic and may be affecting other consumers This also raises questions under the Truth in Lending Act regarding inaccurate or misleading credit advertising, and potential misuse of credit report data under the FCRA. 

Chase told me I was already approved, directed me to accept the terms of the offer which included standard APR language and disclosures ( not apply ), and then denied the application and placed a hard inquiry on several of my credit reports. This is a textbook deceptive practice that harms consumers and can not be justified through fine print disclaimers. 

I request a full investigation into Chases misleading approval messaging and its impact on consumers.

No access to the service that justified the conversion. 
No ability to reverse the transaction.

[ see timeline ] This fraud was reported to Chase when I received the initial phone call about fraud on my account on XX/XX/XXXX [ see phone records of inbound call. ] XX/XX/XXXX Chase sent me a new card, [ see bank statement for new card charge ] but did not close the compromised card, therefore, further fraud was committed on XX/XX/XXXX.

Chase denied my claim stating that a chip-enabled card was present.

After Chases initial denial, I reasonably relied on Chases representations that the transactions were authorized and that the matter was closed. At that time, I was not aware of my specific rights under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E, including my right to request the documents Chase relied upon or to challenge the assumption that a chip-enabled, or card-present denial establishes authorization.
